newsitem.title: UK: UK prompt natgas busy on shortcovering, quiet late.
newsitem.headline: UK prompt natgas busy on shortcovering, quiet late.

text.p: The UK's spot natural gas market saw a spate of prompt activity as buyers looked to cover short positions ahead of the long bank holiday weekend at widely varying prices, but further forward trade was rangebound, dealers said.

One power generator was reported looking for large volumes of gas at the weekend, including possibly as much as 1.5 million therms on Sunday. And there were said to be two other shorts for Sunday, with one trader saying that as much as 2 million therms needed to be covered in total.

But the impact of the extra demand on price was limited, with a trader pointing out that this indicated there were substantial volumes of gas available. Prices on the short term market only went as high as 10.80 pence a therm for next Tuesday. And one dealer reported trading 300,000 therms for Sunday at 10.70 pence a therm, done early in the day.
But as soon as the major positions were covered, prices came off, with trade for Sunday and Monday done at 10.30 pence a therm later in the afternoon.

Further out, the only deals done were within existing ranges. There was good interest for the third quarter, with at least three trades done at 10.50 pence a therm. No deals were confirmed done after the first quarter of next year.
One dealer was surprised by the level of demand for the weekend. "It's strange, with the warmer weather you'd expect demand to come off, I'm surprised prices are so firm," he said.

Demand figures for the weekend are not high. Transco announced that Saturday demand is forecast at 141 mcm, or 33 percent of peak day demand, with the temperature continuing to rise. Transco forecasts 16.3 Celsius for Saturday, against a seasonal normal level of 11.6 Celsius, and against a figure for Friday of 15.4 Celsius.
IPE futures were barely traded, with 40 lots done in three separate deals. The only traded months were August, which fell by 0.01 pence a therm, and April, which was unchanged.
